name: Apply documented transfer threshold over speculation
description: Applies when reviewing a held outbound transfer where the payee roster is unpublished or a corridor may be closed, but a documented reporting-threshold rule is checkable.
procedure:
- Pull case, account, and payee details to gather amount, verification, and jurisdiction.
- Read the transfers policy section for the reporting threshold and its required reason code.
- If the amount exceeds the threshold, escalate with that reason code, even when other concerns exist.
- Do not invent reason codes for unpublished rosters or undocumented corridor closures; apply only rules the docs define and you can verify.
- Issue exactly one decision tool call, then finish.
check: Re-read the workflow's reason-code list and confirm the chosen reason is defined there, and recompute the amount against the documented threshold before trusting the decision.
known_bad: Escalating a transfer whose amount is below the documented reporting threshold as reportable_amount fails this check: the recomputation shows the amount under the threshold and the reason list shows the code applies only above it.

name: Cross-check policy sections before deciding
description: Applies when reviewing an operations ticket whose decision hinges on a rule read from one policy section, to ensure no other policy section adds gating criteria before the decision is issued.
procedure:
- Pull the case details and the account details before consulting policy.
- Read the policy section that directly governs the ticket type.
- Read adjacent policy and workflow sections for additional criteria that could gate the same decision.
- Treat an account or case field as gating only if some section states a rule about it; otherwise it is descriptive.
- Apply the documented rule and issue exactly one decision tool call, then finish.
check: Before trusting the decision, recompute it against every rule found across all sections read: confirm no documented denial condition applies to the account and the requested amount is within the documented cap; also confirm exactly one decision call was made.
known_bad: Approving a request whose amount exceeds the documented approvable cap, or approving while the account meets a documented denial condition (such as a recent chargeback), fails the check because the recomputation against the full set of sections contradicts the decision.

name: Batch independent lookups, ground every claim
description: Applies when resolving a case whose decision requires facts from several independent sources (such as the case record, the account, and the merchant) before any policy rule can be evaluated.
procedure:
- List the facts the decision depends on (case details, account status, merchant category/region) and identify which lookups are independent of each other.
- Issue all independent lookups in a single batched step instead of one at a time.
- Read the policy section that governs the transaction type, then read adjacent sections and the reason-code list to confirm no extra gating criteria apply.
- For each reason code, state explicitly why it does or does not apply using a fetched fact.
- Decide only after every cited fact traces back to an observation.
check: Before acting on the decision, re-scan the transcript: every fact cited in the justification (amount, category, account verification/standing, merchant region) must appear in a tool observation. If any cited fact has no supporting observation, fetch it before deciding.
known_bad: Approving a purchase while citing the account's verification level or standing when no account lookup was ever performed - the check fails because that fact exists nowhere in the observations, so the decision rests on an assumption rather than fetched data.

name: Deny transfer when roster unscreenable
description: Applies when reviewing a pending outbound transfer to a payee that cannot be screened against a restricted-payee roster because the roster is unpublished or otherwise inaccessible.
procedure:
- Gather the case, account, and payee facts, then read the transfers policy and the workflow reason codes.
- Check the amount against the documented reporting threshold and escalate only if it is above.
- Attempt to screen the payee against the restricted roster; note when the roster is unpublished or otherwise unverifiable.
- Treat an unscreenable roster as a failed screen: deny with the documented roster reason (restricted_payee) instead of approving on the assumption that silence means cleared.
- Approve only when the payee screen passes and the amount is below the reporting threshold.
check: Before recording the decision, re-derive it: if the restricted roster could not actually be consulted and the decision is approve, the check fails — change the decision to a denial with the roster reason.
known_bad: Approving a transfer to a payee when the restricted roster could not be checked, on the grounds that the amount is well below the reporting threshold (e.g., roughly a quarter of it) and no other documented rule fires; this was scored wrong, so unscreenable roster must yield a denial regardless of amount.

name: Approve limit increase after gating checks
description: Applies when reviewing a pending limit-increase request where approval depends on account standing and an approvable cap read from policy.
procedure:
- Pull the case record for the requested limit and the account record for standing, verification, and current limit before evaluating any rule.
- Read the policy section on limits and also the reason-code list to catch all gating criteria that could deny the request.
- Deny with the standing reason if the account shows a recent chargeback, whatever the amount.
- Otherwise compare the requested limit against the documented approvable cap: within it, approve; above it, deny with the cap-exceeded reason.
- Do not approve while any gating criterion from the reason-code list remains unchecked.
check: Before approving, recompute each gating condition independently: confirm the account record shows no recent chargeback and restate the numeric comparison of requested limit versus the cap from the policy text; an approval issued while either check fails is invalid.
known_bad: Approving a limit-increase request whose requested amount is numerically above the policy's approvable cap fails this check, because restating the comparison shows the requested limit exceeds the cap and the case must be denied with the cap-exceeded reason.

name: Gate only on documented conditions
description: Applies when deciding a case of one kind (e.g., a transfer, a limit-increase, a card transaction) and an account field or a rule belonging to a different product's policy seems to justify a denial or escalation that the governing policy section does not mention.
procedure:
- Read the policy section that governs the case's kind and list every condition it documents for denying or escalating.
- Treat account fields (credit limits, tenure, open date) as descriptive context unless a governing section states a rule that makes the field gating for this case kind.
- Do not import conditions from other products' rules (e.g., card category instant-approve limits or limit-increase caps) into decisions on other case kinds.
- Evaluate each available reason code only against its documented condition; if none is met, settle with the disposition the grounded facts and in-force rules support rather than inventing a denial reason.
check: Before trusting the decision, recompute each reason code and, for every condition that drove the result, point to the line in the governing section that documents it; if any applied condition comes from a different product's rule or from an undocumented account field, the result is untrusted.
known_bad: Denying an outbound transfer of $9,000 solely because it exceeds the account's documented credit limit of $2,000, when the transfers policy section documents only a roster screen and a reporting threshold and no amount limit — the check fails because no governing section ties the credit limit to transfers.

name: Require roster evidence before restricted_payee
description: Applies when reviewing a pending outbound transfer whose restricted-payee roster cannot be consulted (unpublished or inaccessible), to settle the disposition of the case.
procedure:
- Attempt to screen the payee against the restricted-payee roster before any other evaluation.
- If the roster is unpublished or otherwise inaccessible, the screen cannot be passed: treat the roster screen as failed, not as cleared by silence.
- Deny with reason `restricted_payee`; do not require positive evidence that the payee is on the roster, since inaccessibility itself is the failing condition.
- A below-threshold amount, a verified account, good standing, or an absence of documented corridor closures do not cure the failed screen; evaluate those codes (e.g. `reportable_amount`) only for additional consequences such as escalation, never as grounds to approve past an unscreenable roster.
- Do not let a conflicting documented or remembered rule override this; runs have shown the failing-screen rule is the one in force.
check: Before trusting any approval of an outbound transfer, confirm the payee was actually screened against a roster that was accessible during the run; if the roster was never consultable, the approval is unsupported and must be redone as a denial with `restricted_payee`.
known_bad: Approving a below-threshold transfer from a verified, good-standing account to a business payee in a jurisdiction with no documented corridor closure, where the restricted-payee roster was unpublished and never screened — the check fails on this case, which runs scored wrong.

name: Unscreenable roster is not a restriction
description: Applies when reviewing a pending outbound transfer whose restricted-payee roster cannot be consulted because it is unpublished or otherwise inaccessible.
procedure:
- Gather the case, account, and payee facts in one batch.
- Evaluate every gate the governing transfer policy actually documents (e.g., reporting threshold, account standing) against the gathered facts.
- Treat an inaccessible roster as 'no evidence of restriction', not as a failed screen: the restricted_payee reason requires positive evidence that the payee is listed.
- If no documented gate is violated and there is no affirmative evidence the payee is restricted, approve the transfer.
- Reserve denial for a documented rule violation or a roster entry you have actually seen.
check: Before issuing a restricted_payee denial, point to the specific roster entry or documented statement that names this payee as restricted; if the only basis is that the roster could not be consulted, re-evaluate the remaining documented gates and reconsider approval.
known_bad: A mid-size transfer well under the documented reporting threshold, to a payee with an unrestricted profile, denied solely because the roster was unpublished is scored wrong; the same case is scored correct when approved after the documented gates pass.

name: Unscreenable roster blocks approval
description: Applies when reviewing a pending outbound transfer whose restricted-payee roster cannot be consulted because it is unpublished or otherwise inaccessible.
procedure:
- Gather the case, account, and payee facts before deciding.
- Determine whether the restricted-payee roster can actually be consulted; if it is unpublished or otherwise inaccessible, the payee cannot be screened.
- Deny the transfer with reason restricted_payee: an unscreenable roster is a blocking condition, not evidence that the payee is unrestricted.
- Do not approve on the grounds that no affirmative restriction was found, and do not let account standing, payee profile, or a below-threshold amount override the failed screening; runs show approval of an unscreened transfer scores wrong.
check: Before finalizing, attempt the roster lookup again; if it is still unconsultable, confirm the recorded disposition is a denial with reason restricted_payee, not an approval.
known_bad: Approving a below-threshold transfer from a verified, good-standing account to a business payee in a jurisdiction with no documented corridor closure, where the restricted-payee roster was unpublished and never screened — the check fails on this case, which runs scored wrong; the correct disposition is denial with restricted_payee.

name: Apply documented rule when evidence silent
description: Applies when reviewing a pending card transaction whose category has no scored evidence contradicting the documented policy, so the documented rule is treated as the rule in force.
procedure:
- Batch the case, account, and merchant lookups, then read the governing transactions policy section.
- Search for scored evidence that the documented rule for this category is not the one in force (e.g., an amount documented as approvable that was scored wrong).
- If no such evidence exists, apply the documented rule as written: a category with no listed instant-approve limit has no amount restriction.
- Evaluate each reason code against the grounded facts and require affirmative evidence before firing any practice-based gate.
- Do not import denial conditions (such as the account credit limit) that no governing section lists for card purchases.
check: Before approving, reconfirm that no scored evidence contradicts the documented rule for the category and that no reason code's stated conditions match the case facts.
known_bad: A transaction in a category that has a documented instant-approve limit and for which scored evidence shows approvals above that limit were scored wrong: approving it under the documented limit fails the check because the scored contradiction was not applied.

name: Unscreenable roster means failed screen
description: Applies when reviewing a pending outbound transfer whose restricted-payee roster cannot be consulted because it is unpublished or otherwise inaccessible, and the disposition must be settled despite disagreeing guidance.
procedure:
- Gather the case, account, and payee facts in one batch before reading policy.
- Read the transfers policy and the workflow reason codes.
- Check every other documented gate: reporting threshold, account verification and standing, any affirmative corridor-closure evidence.
- Treat an unconsultable roster as a failed mandatory screen, not a clearance by silence.
- Deny with reason restricted_payee; favorable facts (below threshold, verified account, good standing) do not cure a failed screen.
check: Before recording, re-derive every reason code against the gathered facts and confirm the roster screen is the only failing gate; if any other code also applies or the roster was actually consulted, stop and re-evaluate.
known_bad: Approving a below-threshold transfer from a verified, good-standing account to a business payee solely because the unpublished roster produced no hit — this fails the check, because the screen was assumed clear without evidence rather than shown to pass.

name: Screen payee before threshold escalation
description: Applies when reviewing a held outbound transfer whose amount exceeds a documented reporting threshold while the restricted-payee roster cannot be consulted because it is unpublished or otherwise inaccessible.
procedure:
- Gather case, account, and payee facts in one batch, then read the transfers policy and the workflow reason-code definitions.
- Resolve the payee screen first: if the restricted-payee roster is unpublished or otherwise inaccessible, the screen cannot be completed, so treat the screen as failed and deny with reason restricted_payee.
- Do not fall through to threshold escalation when a gating condition (payee screen) is unresolved; an above-threshold amount does not override an unresolved blocking condition.
- Only when the payee screen actually resolves (roster consulted and payee absent) compare the amount against the documented reporting threshold and escalate with reportable_amount if it is above.
- If both a denial condition and threshold escalation apply, the denial governs; issue one disposition, not the escalation.
check: Before trusting an escalation to reportable_amount, re-read the transfers policy section and confirm the payee screen was actually completed — the roster was consulted and the payee was found absent — not merely unavailable; if the roster was never consultable, the check fails and the disposition must be denial with restricted_payee.
known_bad: A held transfer to a payee under an unpublished-roster regime is escalated as reportable_amount solely because it exceeds the documented reporting threshold; the screen was never completed, so the check fails — the correct disposition is denial with restricted_payee.

name: Check practice-based gates before approving
description: Applies when deciding a case where a policy section grants a blanket clearance (such as no restriction by merchant region, no listed limit, or all categories serviceable) while a reason-code definition ties a blocking condition to current practice rather than to documentation.
procedure:
- Ground the case facts first: amount, category, account standing, and the merchant's region or venue field, using batched lookups.
- Read the governing policy section and the reason-code definitions; list which reason codes are defined by current practice rather than by documentation.
- Treat documented blanket clearances (no listed limit, all categories serviceable, no restriction by region) as NOT evidence that a practice-based condition is absent.
- A case fact matching the practice-based condition is itself affirmative evidence; no separate lookup tool for the condition is required. A run showed a card transaction at a merchant whose region was overseas, denied with the matching practice-based reason code under a documented no-region-restriction clearance, scored 1.
- When the practice-based condition matches, do not approve: deny with the matching reason code (a closed corridor is a hard block, not a manual-review escalation).
- Before finalizing, verify no other reason code fits better (e.g., a category with a documented instant-approve limit, poor account standing, missing verification).
check: Re-read the merchant/account fact that triggered the practice-based condition and confirm it actually matches that condition (e.g., the region field really is overseas or corridor-serving), and that the code fired is the one whose definition names that condition.
known_bad: A card transaction at a merchant whose region is domestic is denied with the corridor reason code because the policy said nothing about regions: rechecking the region fact shows no practice-based condition matches, so the denial is wrong and the transaction should be evaluated on its category limit and account standing alone.

name: Confirm practice-based gates positively
description: Applies when deciding a pending card transaction where a reason-code definition ties a blocking condition to current practice (such as a required verification level or a corridor status) and the account or merchant attribute could trigger it despite a documented blanket clearance.
procedure:
- Read the reason-code definitions and mark which codes are tied to current practice (e.g., verification level, corridor status) rather than to documented policy.
- For each practice-based code, match the grounded account and merchant attributes directly against the code's condition.
- Treat a documented blanket clearance (such as 'available to all account tiers' or 'no category restricted by region') as non-evidence about whether a practice-based gate is satisfied.
- When no scored evidence affirmatively shows the gate is satisfied, follow the disposition the practice-based code implies instead of approving on the documented rule.
- Approve only when every practice-based reason code positively fails to match the facts.
check: Recompute every reason code from its definition against the grounded account and merchant fields; each practice-based gate must be affirmatively shown not to match (e.g., the account's verification level exceeds the gate's requirement) before approving.
known_bad: A basic-verification account makes a purchase in a category the policy clears 'for all account tiers'; approving because no scored evidence contradicts the clearance fails the check, since the verification-level gate was never positively ruled out.

name: Approve transfer when roster unscreenable
description: Applies when reviewing a pending outbound transfer whose restricted-payee roster cannot be consulted because it is unpublished or otherwise inaccessible, so the mandatory payee screen cannot be run.
procedure:
- Gather case, account, and payee facts, and read the transfers policy section.
- Apply the documented reporting threshold: a transfer at or below it does not fire reportable_amount.
- If the restricted-payee roster is unpublished or otherwise cannot be consulted, the mandatory screen is incomplete; deny the transfer with reason restricted_payee.
- Do not require affirmative evidence that the payee is listed; the inability to run the screen is itself the blocking condition.
- Do not approve a transfer whose mandatory screen could not be run, regardless of account verification, standing, tenure, payee type, or amount relative to the threshold.
- A scored run showed that a below-threshold transfer from a verified, good-standing account to a business payee was approved solely because the roster was unpublished and scored 0, so treat denial with restricted_payee as the disposition in force whenever the screen cannot be run.
check: Before recording any disposition other than denied/restricted_payee, verify that the restricted-payee screen actually ran against a consultable roster; if no roster observation exists, recompute the disposition as denied with restricted_payee.
known_bad: A transfer below the documented reporting threshold from a verified, good-standing account to a business payee, approved because the roster was unpublished, is wrong; the check fails because no roster consultation ever occurred, so the mandatory screen is incomplete and the disposition must be denied with restricted_payee.

name: Trust documented clearance over inferred gates
description: Applies when deciding a pending card transaction where a workflow reason-code description (e.g., a corridor closed 'under current practice') seems to match an account or merchant attribute while the governing policy section grants a blanket clearance for that attribute.
procedure:
- Ground the case facts (account attributes, merchant attributes, amount) and read the governing policy section plus the reason-code definitions.
- Note the blanket clearance in the policy section and the practice-based wording of the reason code.
- Before approving on the clearance, search the skill library for directly scored evidence that the practice-based blocking condition fires for an attribute matching this case's facts.
- If such scored evidence exists (a like case with the same attribute, the same reason code, and the same documented clearance scored as correct), deny with the matching reason code; the scored evidence ties this case's attributes to the block.
- If no such scored evidence exists, treat the clearance as in force and approve; do not infer the gate fires from the reason code's 'current practice' wording plus a matching attribute alone.
- Rule out the remaining reason codes individually: amount against documented category limits, verification level, account standing, any other gate's stated condition.
check: Re-verify that the cited scored case's attribute, reason code, and documented clearance all match the current case's facts, and that every other reason code's stated condition positively fails to match; a denial is trusted only then.
known_bad: A card purchase in a category with a documented instant-approve limit is denied with the corridor reason code because a prior scored case about a different attribute (e.g., merchant region) was cited as evidence; the check fails because the cited case's blocking attribute does not match and a better-fitting code was skipped.

name: Over-limit escalation needs positive evidence
description: Applies when reviewing a pending card transaction whose amount exceeds the documented category instant-approve limit, to decide whether the documented limit alone justifies an over_limit escalation.
procedure:
- Gather the case, account, and merchant facts before evaluating any rule.
- Read the documented category instant-approve limit and note whether the amount exceeds it.
- Treat the documented limit as unverified: scored runs show that escalating a purchase somewhat above a documented category limit (for example, a purchase about 25% over a documented electronics limit, on a verified good-standing account) was scored wrong, so the limit actually in force is higher than the documented one in such cases.
- Do not escalate with over_limit on documentation alone; settle the case per the remaining policy only if no positive source contradicts approval.
- Before finalizing, check the other gates (verification level, account standing, corridor status, merchant region, restricted payee) for any condition positively evidenced in the run.
check: Before escalating with over_limit, confirm a positive in-run source (a scored outcome, a tool result, or an explicit statement of the limit in force) that the applicable limit is below the transaction amount; if only the policy document states the limit, the escalation is unsupported and must not be issued.
known_bad: A pending card transaction roughly a quarter above its category's documented instant-approve limit, on a verified good-standing account at a domestic merchant, escalated with over_limit solely because the policy document lists that limit - the check fails because no positive evidence establishes that the documented limit is the one in force.

name: Escalate above threshold despite unscreenable roster
description: Applies when reviewing a held outbound transfer whose amount exceeds the documented reporting threshold while the restricted-payee roster cannot be consulted because it is unpublished or otherwise inaccessible.
procedure:
- Read the transfers policy section and record the documented reporting threshold and the screening rule.
- Confirm the restricted-payee roster cannot be consulted (unpublished or inaccessible) and that no accessible evidence shows this payee is on it.
- Compare the transfer amount against the documented threshold; if it exceeds the threshold, escalate the case with the reason code for a reportable amount.
- Do not deny with the restricted-payee reason code when the roster is merely unavailable: runs scored that disposition wrong, so an unrun screen does not override the threshold rule in force.
check: Recompute the threshold comparison from the policy value and the case amount, and confirm the chosen disposition is escalation with the reportable-amount reason code; if the disposition is denial with the restricted-payee code, the check fails because no roster entry was ever produced to substantiate the restriction.
known_bad: An above-threshold transfer to a payee with no accessible restricted listing is denied with the restricted-payee reason code solely because the roster is unpublished; the check fails because the amount exceeds the documented threshold and no roster entry supports the denial.

name: Practice-based gate needs positive match
description: Applies when deciding a pending card transaction where a practice-based reason code (e.g., one tied to a verification level or corridor status) could be read to fire on an account or merchant attribute, but no documentation or scored evidence states the threshold that attribute must fail.
procedure:
- Gather the case, account, and merchant facts before evaluating any reason code.
- For each practice-based reason code, deny only when its blocking requirement is documented, or scored evidence shows this exact attribute matches the blocking condition.
- An attribute that merely might fall below an unstated threshold (e.g., the lowest verification tier when no minimum is documented) does not match the gate; absence of proof of passing is not proof of failing.
- If no reason code affirmatively matches and the governing policy section grants a clearance for the attribute, approve.
check: Before denying on a practice-based gate, cite the documentation or scored evidence that states the requirement the attribute fails; if no such requirement can be cited, reverse the denial and approve under the documented clearance.
known_bad: A lowest-tier-verification account makes a purchase in a category the policy clears for all accounts, with no documentation stating a minimum verification level; denying with the verification reason code fails the check because no requirement is shown to be violated.

name: Resolve conflicting skills by grounding
description: Applies when the skill library contains contradictory guidance for the same case type (e.g., some entries say deny, others approve or escalate) and the agent must choose a tie-breaking method before deciding.
procedure:
- Group the conflicting skills by the disposition they recommend; for each side, record what scored-run evidence it cites.
- If one side cites scored-run outcomes and the other side does not, follow the side that does.
- If both sides cite scored-run outcomes, compare each side's `check` and `known_bad` case shape against the current case's attributes (e.g., amount relative to a documented threshold, account verification and standing, payee type); prefer the side whose `known_bad` case matches the current case most closely.
- Weight corroboration: a rule stated consistently in the checks of several independent skills counts for more than a lone contrary entry, even when the lone entry cites scored evidence.
- Decide with the winning side and record which evidence and which matching `known_bad` grounded the choice.
check: Before trusting the chosen disposition, verify that the losing side's `known_bad` case does not match the current case's attributes better than the winning side's; if it does, switch to the losing side and re-derive the decision before recording it.
known_bad: Two conflicting skills each cite scored runs and recommend opposite dispositions for the same case type; an agent breaks the tie by counting citations or names instead of comparing each side's `known_bad` case shape to the case attributes, and picks the side whose `known_bad` case (e.g., a differing amount band, account standing, or payee type) does not match the current case — the side whose `known_bad` matches exactly is the one in force, so the check fails on the chosen disposition.

name: Don't trust documented spend limits
description: Applies when reviewing a pending card transaction whose amount is compared against a documented category instant-approve limit, to settle approve-versus-over_limit using scored evidence of which limit is actually in force.
procedure:
- Read the documented category limit and treat it as unverified, not as the limit in force.
- Scan the skill library for scored cases in the same category and convert each into a numeric bound: a known_bad escalation that was scored wrong proves an approval of that amount was correct, giving a lower bound on the in-force limit; any scored-correct escalation gives an upper bound.
- If no scored case in that category exists, fall back to the documented rule: at or below the limit approve, above it escalate with over_limit.
- If scored bounds exist, approve when the amount is at or below the highest proven-approvable amount; escalate over_limit only when the amount exceeds every proven-approvable bound.
- Independently check practice-based reason codes (verification, corridor, standing) and gate only on attributes that documented policy or scored evidence affirmatively matches; do not deny on an unstated threshold.
check: Recompute the disposition against the bounds before acting: an approval requires the amount to be at or below the highest proven-approvable amount derived from a scored case in the same category, and an escalation requires the amount to be above all such bounds; verify by restating the bound, the amount, and which side of it the amount falls on.
known_bad: A purchase in a documented-limit category is approved at an amount that exceeds the highest proven-approvable bound in that category (for example, approving $540 against a documented $500 limit when the only scored evidence is a scored-wrong escalation of $505, proving only $505 approvable) — the bound check fails because the approval is not covered by the scored evidence.
